references.text: Parallel account of the consecration of Aaron and his sons to the priesthood, with the same sacrifices described here.
The requirement that the sacrificial animal must be without blemish (תָּמִים) from the herd is repeated here.
Elaborates on the requirement that sacrificial animals must be without blemish (תְּמִימִם) to be accepted.
Earlier reference to consecrating (לְקַדֵּשׁ) Aaron and his sons for priestly service.
Similar consecration procedure for the Levites using a bull and rams.
The book of Hebrews refers to the consecration of Old Testament priests and contrasts this with Christ's perfect priesthood.
Refers to the consecration rituals and the use of blood in the old covenant.
The execution of the priestly consecration commanded here.
Ezekiel restores the purification ritual from the Mosaic law (bull and ram) for the service of the new temple.
Direct allusion to the priestly consecration ritual to criticize incorrect cultic practices.
